Section E lists both published times for the Blyth-Eccles-Stella West trip, which conflict, without resolving them; since bundle 1.1.0 there is no compiler's note pointing out the conflict (readers compare the two times themselves). S04.construction: Synthesised account in two parts. Part 1 is a role-level, chronological shift narrative restating only published facts (ESO 4.2 Little Barford, the RWE SOE in APP Appendix E, Ofgem 3.25-3.29); no names, conversations, readings or clock times are added and no illustrative values are used. Part 2 gives attributed post-event statements, each in its source's order: the RWE preliminary findings dated 30 August 2019 (UPS, steam turbine, gas turbines) and Ofgem 3.28-3.29 dated 3 January 2020, as verbatim quotes or close paraphrase. Since bundle 1.1.0 the account carries no builder classification (no known/not known, established/not established or hypothesis labels); the sources' own words ('RWE's hypothesis is', 'is ongoing', 'For reasons presently unknown', 'We have established', 'has not been established', 'preliminary view') carry the epistemic status. Deliberately not carried into the pack (flagged for the domain reviewer, criteria D4.3/D4.4): the ESO executive summary (PDF page 4) says the GT1A trip was 'due to high pressure in the steam bypass system following the failure of a bypass valve to operate correctly'. ESO section 4.2 (PDF page 20) and RWE (APP page 46) give the excursion's cause as 'presently unknown', and Ofgem 3.29 states that the root cause of the high pressure conditions has not been established, so the pack keeps it unknown. A submission that asserts a bypass-valve failure as established is not supported by the visible evidence.
